output.brief: I can't yet say what is driving store 14's rise, and the evidence doesn't justify pulling the self-checkout lanes, hiring a guard or disciplining anyone. The Q1–Q3 shrink figures are estimates from partial cycle counts, with an error band of about ±0.6 points per quarter. The store's 0.8-point rise is close to that band. Across the chain, two straight interim rises were confirmed by the year-end count only 13 times out of 27. The rise in recorded shoplifting incidents is chain-wide. It coincides with the new incident app launched on 1 April, while chain shrink stayed flat, so it says little about store 14. The ethics-line tip was checked against CCTV and showed bale runs to the compactor, so it doesn't support staff theft. Sales mix hasn't shifted. Neighbouring stores without self-checkout show no similar rise. That doesn't clear self-checkout, but it doesn't implicate it either. Next steps: refuse the proposal to drop store 14 from the 7 December count. That count is the only reliable measurement, and skipping it would remove the check on the very question you're asking. Confirm the store stays in the count by 20 November. Hold spending and personnel action until the full-count result is compared with the interim figures. If the count confirms a real rise, then investigate self-checkout, receiving and staff. I'm moderately confident in this.
